title: signerKey routes a broadcast to the right persona and the ledger attributes it
notes: 0.28.0 keyring + 0.32.0 attribution. Until 0.34.0 NOTHING in the suite passed signerKey: the orchestrator blanks DEXE_PRIVATE_KEY in the MCP child so composites return payloads, then signs them with its own ethers Wallet — leaving the SignerManager per-(chain,address) nonce queue, attachBroadcastRecorder attribution, withBroadcastLock and the agent ledger completely dark. Step 2 is the one step in the whole suite that crosses the server's broadcast path end-to-end, and it is deliberately the cheapest possible write: ERC20.approve(UserKeeper, 0) on the fixture's own gov token — a no-op allowance, ~$0.01 on chain 97. Step 3 pins the unknown-slot refusal. AGENT_PK_1..8 / AGENT_FUNDER_PK reach the keyring as agent1..agent8 / funder through the DEXE_AGENT_PK_* aliases in src/config.ts, so no extra env is needed.

steps.comment: approve(spender=0x…dEaD, amount=0) — the cheapest well-formed ERC20 write, and a non-zero spender so a token that rejects the zero address still accepts it. The point is WHO signed it, not what it did. 0x095ea7b3 = ERC20.approve(address,uint256); not on the GovUserKeeper denylist.
Raw signerKey arg, NOT serverSign — the point is that an unknown slot is refused by name.

successCriteria.check: sent.signerKey == 'agent1' and sent.from == the AGENT_PK_1 address
the ledger reports a window, a spend total and a budget for agent1
badSlot error lists the configured keyring slots
